assets.label: Cash, interbank and central bank deposits

liabilities.label: Bank deposits, repos and bonds issued

balance.note: A bank's balance sheet is mostly other people's money: customer deposits fund the loans. Shareholders' funds are about 9% of assets, which is why capital ratios matter.

safety.label: CET1 capital ratio
safety.plain: The bank's own capital as a cushion against losses, as a share of its risk-weighted loans. Bank Negara's minimum is 4.5% plus buffers. As printed in the report's capital note; some banks print it before deducting the proposed dividend.

safety.label: Total capital ratio
safety.plain: All qualifying capital as a share of risk-weighted loans; the regulatory minimum is 8% plus buffers.

safety.label: Gross impaired loans
safety.plain: Loans in trouble as a share of all loans. Lower is better.

safety.label: Loan loss allowance coverage
safety.plain: Money already set aside for losses, compared with the troubled loans. Above 100% means fully covered.

safety.label: Loan to deposit ratio
safety.plain: The bank lends out about RM110 of every RM100 deposited.

safety.label: CASA ratio
safety.plain: Share of deposits in current and savings accounts, which pay little interest and keep funding cheap.

safety.label: Liquidity coverage ratio
safety.plain: Cash and easy-to-sell assets against 30 days of stressed outflows; the minimum is 100%.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM5.0 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: You pay about RM10 for every RM1 of yearly profit. A high number means investors expect growth.

metrics.label: EPS (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: Profit earned for each share you own over the last year.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (dividends paid in the last 12 months)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 of shares, about RM4.5 a year comes back as cash dividends.

metrics.label: Payout ratio
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 profit, about RM45 is paid out; the rest is kept to grow.

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 0.4 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 shareholders have in the company, it earned about RM4 profit last year.

metrics.label: Net margin 9M2026
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM18.90.

metrics.label: Revenue growth 9M2026
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Profit growth 9M2026
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Cost to income (9M2026)
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 of income, about RM64 is spent on staff, branches and IT. Lower is more efficient.

metrics.label: Credit cost (9M2026, annualised)
metrics.plain: Provisions for bad loans equal to 0.37% of loans a year. Lower is better.

drivers.evidence: Loans grew 14.1% in the year to September 2026 (database)
drivers.why: More than twice the industry pace.

drivers.evidence: Net income rose 14.0% to RM1.99bn in 9M2026 (Q B1)
Provisions of RM224m in 9M2026 against RM9m a year earlier (database)
Deposits grew only 1.0% while loans grew 14.1% (database)
drivers.why: Funding the gap gets more expensive.

drivers.evidence: Management flags persistent margin compression from competition for deposits (Q B3)
drivers.why: Squeezes what it earns on each loan.
Below its cost of capital; why it trades below book value.

outlook.text: Malaysia's GDP growth targeted at around 5.0% in 2027, backed by domestic demand and exports (Q B3).
Persistent net interest margin compression from competition for deposits and rising yields (Q B3).
Agile but cautious posture; stricter credit governance and portfolio monitoring (Q B3).

outlookOverall.text: Management is cautious: growth with disciplined balance-sheet management amid margin pressure (Q B3).
